Hi!

> SQLAlchemy's asyncpg dialect uses prepared statements for all statements, except this particular ping.

You won't believe how I was surprised when I was reading the discussion in provided commit after I caught this error 😅
Anyway, I attached a script with this error

> also, I dont understand why you would be using connection pooling with pgbouncer. shouldn't you use NullPool in any case?

To use NullPool means to loose benefits from pooling: no limits on creating connections on client side, overhead on creation and etc. So I think it is not meaningless.

> test case passes without error:

Did you run it with pgbouncer in transactional mode?

issue.body:
Hi!

I use sqlalchemy 1.4  with asyncpg driver with pgbouncer.

```python

    from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine
    from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
    from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

    engine = create_async_engine(
        f'postgresql+asyncpg://{username}:{password}@{host}:{port}/{dbname}',
        echo=False,
    )
    session_maker = sessionmaker(
        engine,
        class_=AsyncSession,
    )


```

I have an error:

```
asyncpg.exceptions.DuplicatePreparedStatementError: prepared statement "__asyncpg_stmt_a__" already exists
HINT:
NOTE: pgbouncer with pool_mode set to "transaction" or
"statement" does not support prepared statements properly.
You have two options:

* if you are using pgbouncer for connection pooling to a
  single server, switch to the connection pool functionality
  provided by asyncpg, it is a much better option for this
  purpose;

* if you have no option of avoiding the use of pgbouncer,
  then you can set statement_cache_size to 0 when creating
  the asyncpg connection object.
```

How i can pass this setting (statement_cache_size=0) to asyncpg connection object?

body:
**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**place asyncpg do_ping within a transaction if one not begun already** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4814

asyncpg isn't able to reliably run statements without there being a transaction present, which guards against the connection changing underneath while it tries to run the steps to emit our command.    so we add a transaction to ping which is effectively what all the other drivers do already.
1.4 does not have this issue since it uses `select 1` using the normal execute, correct?

There seems to be no advantage to using a client-side pool and additionally pgbouncer on top.

You should specify `poolclass=NullPool,` to let pgbouncer do all the work instead of the client.

And there is also no need to use the `pool_pre_ping=True,` because pgbouncer already does it for you (see [server_check_delay and server_check_query parameters](https://www.pgbouncer.org/config.html))

I think it mostly depends on the deployment / connection requirements. When using tls etc creating a new connection requires several round trips, so it may still make sense keeping connections in the pool on the client
